title: ProPerAgent: Toward Memory-Driven Proactive Assistance
abstract: arXiv:2610.22671v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As assistants move from reactive answering toward proactive intervention, memory changes role: it no longer only supplies the answer to a query, it determines whether and when to speak at all. Prior work in this setting hands the system the relevant fact in context; we study the regime that makes the problem hard, where the evidence justifying an intervention must be mined from a long-horizon personal memory. We introduce ProPerMem, a benchmark for memory-driven proactive assistance (MPA), pairing egocentric video with year-long, distractor-rich user memories (~618K tokens on average), human-verified trigger windows, and a protocol that scores content and timing jointly. Every baseline we evaluate performs poorly (at most 15%), including frontier models given summarized or retrieval-augmented memory. translated_title: ProPerAgent：迈向记忆驱动的主动性助手
translated_abstract: 随着助手从被动应答转向主动干预，记忆的角色发生了变化：它不再仅仅为查询提供答案，而是决定了系统是否以及何时该开口说话。以往在这一设定下的工作是把相关事实直接放进上下文中交给系统；我们研究的是使问题真正困难的情形，即证明干预合理性的证据必须从长时段的个人记忆中挖掘出来。我们提出了ProPerMem，一个面向记忆驱动主动性助手（MPA）的基准，它将第一人称视角视频与长达一年、充满干扰信息的用户记忆（平均约618K token）、经人工验证的触发窗口，以及一个对内容与时机进行联合评分的协议相配对。我们评估的所有基线模型表现都很差（最高仅15%），包括在给定摘要式或检索增强记忆的情况下的前沿模型。一项受控研究解释了原因：当神谕证据在触发窗口内直接提供时，GPT-5.3-Chat能达到96%；而让它自行选择证据时性能则大幅下降
tldr: 该论文提出ProPerMem基准，首次要求AI助手从长达一年、充满干扰的个人记忆中自主挖掘证据来决定是否及何时主动介入，发现现有模型（含前沿模型）表现极差（最高仅15%），而提供现成证据时性能可达96%，揭示了记忆证据挖掘是主动性助手的核心瓶颈。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces ProPerMem, a benchmark for memory-driven proactive assistance requiring agents to mine intervention-justifying evidence from year-long, distractor-rich personal memories, showing current frontier models fail badly (≤15%) while oracle evidence boosts GPT-5.3-Chat to 96%, identifying memory mining as the core bottleneck.
